prompt.text:
You are designing a feature for The Adventures of Tom. This session is DESIGN ONLY. You will not change the game, the engine, any data file, the Battle Guide page, or run any paid generation. You will produce a plan document, a visual mock, and the build cards that follow from them.

READ FIRST, in this order: CLAUDE.md, claude/handoff-rules.md, data/board.json. Then say in your first line that this is a new card (Board: new card c-movebench-design). Your first push is that card plus the commit "board: start c-movebench-design". The card: lane claude, col prog, theme "Battle Animations", tag "movebench-design", title "Design the Move Workbench in the Battle Guide", after "nothing for Tom: see the Tom card t-movebench-plan", and prompt.text equal to the text of this message with the usual model and effort fields (Claude Fable 5.2, high). Run python3 tools/board_check.py before pushing. Other sessions push often: fetch and rebase before pushing, never push conflict markers. The clone is shallow; if a rebase replays commits that are not yours, fetch --depth=50 and use rebase --onto.

WHAT TOM WANTS (his words, 2026-11-26): "I don't wanna do any more automatic videos because of the quality issues. I'm gonna curate them all myself, but I need a way to do it, and I think that the battle guide is the best place to do it in the animations tab, so we need to make sure for every single animation that I am able to configure every single variable required in order to do this move and then potentially even preview the move entirely. And remember this move needs to include not only its original animation but special effects, objects, etc, exactly as specified in our spec."

So the goal is a MOVE WORKBENCH inside ADMIN > BATTLE GUIDE > Animations. For every animation Tom opens one page where he can set every variable that makes the move, and press Preview to see the whole composed move (body video, stage, objects, effects, timing) exactly as the game will play it. He judges by looking; he does not code and must never be asked to edit a file or choose between implementation options.

FACTS CHECKED ON 2026-11-26 (verify each before relying on it; correct me where the repo disagrees):
- The Guide (battle-guide.html, docs/BATTLE_GUIDE.md, data/guide-anims.json with about 346 animations) already does the BODY VIDEO: per animation a prompt, Make this video (one tap, Wan 3.0 for family at $0.50, xAI Grok lite for monsters), start picture make or upload, Update the prompt from a note, take comparison against the clip in the game, Use this one, Keep the old one, Send a note. State is rows in queue.json on branch guideq, written by tools/guidegen/. Its Manifest panel (data/guide-manifest.json, tools/guidegen/manifest_crosswalk.py) is READ ONLY: it shows what the manifests plan and what is done.
- It does NOT let Tom set: the start frame and which prop is held versus worn (the board shows 7 two-held-prop decisions waiting); timing (contact moment, hit stop, approach and return slides; these come from the manifest numbers via engine/guide-timing.js and data/pass1-meta.js, applied by code in engine/pass1-vfx.js); stage steps (data/b3-stage.js, the B3_STAGE rows: tier, budget, body {clip, job, keep, marks}, hit, steps, lasting, setpiece, assets, size, played by engine/b3-stage.js, written today only by Claude sessions; a move with no row shows "Waits for staging"); effects (the manifests name them, art-factory/aot-stage2c-vfx-library-v11.json holds 37 assets with params, sfxHook and previewStyle, all buildStatus todo; the effects that draw today are code-drawn in engine/b3-vfx.js with no settings on any page); Capstone set pieces; sound.
- Preview today: the Guide's player shows the body video only (plus the lava ground effect). "In a fight" opens a real Battle 3 fight with the move used first (engine/b3-lab.js, cfg.first) but nothing can be changed there. engine/b3-movelab.js (Move Lab) covers only Tom's eight moves with Keep, Tweak, Replace. Battle Lab > PASS-1 DRAFT REVIEW covers seven moves for five people.
- The move manifests are art-factory/aot-stage2-pass{1,2,3}-manifest-24fps.json (123 moves, 24 fps, each with a motion text and an engineSpec). Their stylePrefix and negativePrompt are banned by the Pipeline Lock and are not used.
- Animation kinds in the Guide (ids): body:(owner):(state), move:(skill id), act:(foe):(act), wind:(foe):(act). Family members are in the new battle (Battle 3) only; Battle 2 is being deleted and is out of scope.

HARD CONSTRAINTS (all in CLAUDE.md; read them, do not paraphrase them into something weaker):
- Battle Animation Pipeline Lock and art-factory/PIPELINE_LOCK.json: never weaken. Direct-Hero start frames. One held prop per Wan clip, any other prop is worn and its effect is a Battle Lab effect.
- No painted poses in battle: battle animation is video from a video model. A still is only a start or end picture input.
- No breathing in the overworld or scenes.
- Battle rules never wait on an animation (Battle 3 resolves the result first and plays beats; a clip only calls reveal(share)). Keep that seam: a move with no spec still plays with the defaults.
- Images only in the Art Library (an effect or prop picture Tom needs is an Art Library entry he generates there; never a prompt for an outside AI).
- No API keys on any admin page. Anything that needs a secret is a request committed to the repo and fulfilled by an Action (see keysecrets1). The one exception is the saved GitHub token the pages already use (aot-gh-token).
- Purge replaced files completely: the plan must say what each phase deletes when the new spec replaces the old thing (B3_STAGE rows, pass1-meta, guide-timing, code-drawn effects), so nothing is kept as a fallback.
- Phone first. The Guide has four layouts (docs/DUO.md: 466 x 657, 678 x 445, 951 x 648, 669 x 869) plus the 3440 x 1440 monitor in the Admin Dashboard. The workbench must work at all of them.
- No automatic or bulk video generation is part of this feature. Do not design a path that spends money without Tom's tap. The existing board bulk path (wan-gen --bulk, c-wanstop cards, t-wangaveup cards) is a separate matter: list in the plan what it should do next (keep, pause or retire) as a recommendation, and do not touch it.

WHAT TO PRODUCE (all in this repo, none of it in the Project):
1. claude/movebench-plan.md. It must contain, each as its own section:
   a. INVENTORY. Read the three manifests, the effect library, b3-stage.js, b3-stage engine, b3-vfx.js, guide-timing, pass1-vfx, pass1-meta, b3-movelab and the Guide's player. Produce the complete table of every variable that today shapes a move, where it lives, who sets it, and whether Tom can reach it. Derive the list from the files; do not guess. Include monster acts and wind-ups, body states (idle, guard, hit, dodge, knocked out, victory, running), counters, the Family Ruckus moves (univ-double-team, univ-full-ruckus) and Capstone set pieces. Say plainly which animation kinds need which sections.
   b. THE SPEC. One per-animation spec file format that becomes the single source of truth for the engine, the Guide and the preview, so the preview and the game cannot disagree. Give the exact schema (every field, type, range, default, which variables Tom sets and which are derived), a worked example for one Basic, one Skill with a held prop, one Capstone with a set piece, and one monster act. Say how a move with no spec behaves. Say how it replaces B3_STAGE, pass1-meta and the manifest-derived timing, in what order, and how every existing move migrates without a regression (name the tests that prove it).
   c. PREVIEW. How Preview composes the whole move (body video, stage steps, objects, effects, hit stop, shake, sound cues) by running the SAME engine code the game runs, not a second implementation. Say where it runs (inside the Guide page, a stub fight, or the real fight), why, how it loads without pulling every clip into phone memory (about 10 MB per clip), how it handles a move whose video does not exist yet (it must still preview stage and effects against the idle video), and how Tom scrubs, slows and loops it. Preview is free.
   d. THE PAGE. The workbench screen for one animation: sections, order, what is editable, what each control is, how a change is saved, undone and versioned, how Tom sees "this move is finished" and who set that (his approval state per animation, replacing today's NOTE OPEN and Keep, Tweak, Replace verbs where they overlap), how the list shows progress across 346 animations, and how the existing Make this video flow, takes and Use this one fit inside it unchanged. Controls must be plain words, not codes.
   e. EFFECTS AND OBJECTS. How each of the 37 library assets is configured per move from the params the library already defines, how a missing asset or prop picture is requested (Art Library entry, then it appears), and how an unbuilt effect is previewed (a labelled placeholder that is clearly not final).
   f. SAVING. Where specs live and how the page writes them. Weigh the precedents (queue.json on a branch with compare and swap, data/script-edits.json on main, the board's ghBoard and storeUpdate) against size limits (GitHub sends no content over 1 MiB), concurrent edits by Tom and by sessions, and how a saved spec reaches the game build and the cache tags. Pick one and justify it.
   g. BUILD PHASES. A numbered list of phases, each small enough for one Sonnet 5.5 medium session, in dependency order, each with: what it builds, what it deletes, the tests, how Tom can judge it, and the model and effort by the logic in claude/handoff-rules.md (Fable only where the rules allow it, with the reason). Phase 1 must deliver something Tom can use on his phone.
   h. RISKS AND WHAT I CHECKED. What could go wrong, what you verified in the repo versus assumed, and anything you could not check.
   The plan makes the calls. Do not hand Tom options. If a decision truly cannot be undone and could reasonably go either way, ask one short question about it in the Tom card, nowhere else.
2. claude/movebench-mock/: a visual mock of the workbench Tom can judge before anything is built (static HTML and images; follow how claude/dashboard-mock/ was done). Show one Basic, one held-prop Skill, one Capstone and one monster act at the four Duo sizes and at 3440 x 1440. Look at your own mock at every size and fix what is wrong before pushing.
3. The build cards: one Claude card per phase in the plan, in order, each with the full prompt as handoff-rules.md requires (what, before steps, model, effort, text ending "Attach trivituso81/adventures-of-tom with push access (add_repo)."), each queued behind the Tom card below.
4. One Tom card, id t-movebench-plan, ask decide, choices 2 to 4 (first one is yours and ends "(Recommended)", one leads line each: approve the plan and mock as written, approve with changes he types, or stop). Its next names the exact files to open (claude/movebench-plan.md and the mock path, and how he views them) and says it blocks the first build card. Follow the board3 and board4 rules in CLAUDE.md for Tom cards.
5. docs/CHANGES.md: a "## movebench-design (date): ..." heading and a short entry. Rebuild the claude index (python3 tools/claude_index.py). Run bump_tags per the build label rule, python3 tools/board_check.py --push movebench-design, and python3 tools/smoke.py (it passes on main today; it must still).

HOW TO WORK:
- The repo is large (battle-guide.html is about 157 KB, docs/BATTLE_GUIDE.md about 81 KB, engine files up to 400 KB). Search and read the sections you need; never open a whole big file. This is one task in one conversation: do not wander into unrelated work.
- If you fail at the same thing twice in a row, stop and follow the STOP-LOSS RULE in the project instructions.
- Ground every claim in a file you read. Where the plan states a number or a name, it must match the repo.

HOW TO REPORT (CLAUDE.md "How every reply to Tom is shaped"): first line, what you did in the past tense, with the commit and tag pushed and what you did not do. Right below, the exact steps Tom takes next (open the Tom card t-movebench-plan on the board, the files to look at, the button to tap). No options lists. Then one line each for the decisions you made. Define any technical term. No em dashes in anything you write for him or put in a file. End with "Theme: Battle Animations. Pending your action: yes."

prompt.text: Read CLAUDE.md, claude/handoff-rules.md and claude/movebench-plan.md (the whole of sections b to f once, then the row of this phase in section g and the Built notes of the phases before it), and look at the pictures in claude/movebench-mock/ (README.md lists them; the .html files beside it hold every drawn size and colour). Read cards c-movebench-11 and t-movebench-plan in data/board.json: Tom's answer and note on t-movebench-plan come first, and a change he typed that touches this phase is applied to the plan and the mock before you build. Your first push is the commit board: start c-movebench-11. Phase 11 (d.1 rows 5 and 7, b.2 stage.lasting, stage.setpiece and answer). Lasting things: while which status, on whom, how it enters, how it answers a react or intercept beat, how it leaves. When it answers: the counter video (the 7 counter clips of the manifests) made through the same Make this video flow as a row of its own, and the effects that play with it. The Set piece section: length (3 to 10 s), how dark the field goes (Off, Dusk, Night and in between), its steps with the same step editor. tools/movebench/page_test.py: a ward's object enters, answers a monster attack in the preview and leaves; a set piece's length and dim change the run. Rules that hold for every phase: the preview and the game run the same engine files, never a second implementation; a move with no spec plays the defaults and the battle rules never wait on an animation; no painted poses in battle; never weaken art-factory/PIPELINE_LOCK.json or the lock files; no API key on any page; images only in the Art Library; no step may make a video or spend money without Tom's tap, and a session never runs a paid generation; phone first, at 466 x 657, 678 x 445, 951 x 648 and 669 x 869; purge what the phase replaces and grep for zero references. Look at every picture your tests write before you push. Run python3 tools/smoke.py. Add a short Built notes block for this phase under section g of claude/movebench-plan.md (what was built, what differs from the plan and why, what the next phase must know), update docs/BATTLE_GUIDE.md, write the docs/CHANGES.md heading and run bump_tags. Build name movebench11. This phase hands Tom a card: in the same push add the Tom card t-movebench-11-try (lane tom, ask play, fyi true, title "Stage a move from start to finish") with these steps as its next: Open ADMIN > BATTLE GUIDE > Animations > Tom > Tarmac Porsche Transfer. Change one step of its set piece, add words on screen, add one effect and change its settings, and add a new object (it shows as a pink box until you make its picture in the Art Library). Save draft, then Finished. Press All good, or Something is wrong and say what you tried and what you saw. Then set after on c-movebench-11 to t-movebench-11-try. The next card, c-movebench-12, starts when this build ships. Attach trivituso81/adventures-of-tom with push access (add_repo).
